chunks: As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Mūsā ibn Bakr, from al-Fuḍayl ibn Yasār, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام.
That a man from among the Muslims became a Christian, so he was brought to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام. He asked him to repent, but he refused, so he seized him by his hair and then said:
“Trample him, O servants of Allah.” So he was trampled until he died.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: the title of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام, acting as the governing authority
key_terms.تَنَصَّرَ: became a Christian; apostatized from Islam to Christianity
key_terms.فَاسْتَتَابَهُ: he sought his repentance; he asked him to return and repent

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith in Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām say about the punishment of an apostate who refuses to repent?
ai.summary: This report narrates that a Muslim man apostatized and was brought before Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام. After being asked to repent and refusing, an order was given that resulted in his death. The passage is cited in the context of legal rulings concerning the apostate.
